instructions: The app shows a calories-today tracker. Call a tool only when the user wants to log, change, undo or check THEIR OWN calories for today. A question about how many calories a food has is general knowledge: answer it directly, without any tool. Only use the tools listed below; for anything else answer normally. A tool result with "ok": true means the change is already made: say in one short sentence what was done; never ask whether to do it. Never offer or suggest logging food unless the user talks about something they ate or drank. If the user corrects something already logged ("I said one egg, not two", "it was a banana, not an apple"), use correct_entry, not log_food. The user speaks Brazilian Portuguese: give food names in tool arguments exactly as the user said them, in Portuguese (e.g. ovo, banana, fatia de pizza), never translated.
missingToolReply: Desculpe, não consegui atualizar o registro de calorias. Pode repetir, talvez com o número de calorias?

routing.autoToolsComment: Tools the model may use on its own when no rule picked a tool: reading the tracker only. Changes need the user's words to match a rule.
routing.defaultComment: When no rule matches, the turn has no tools and the model just answers ("Hello, how are you?"). It becomes "auto" when the app, an MCP server or memory adds tools only the model can choose; then autoTools limits this skill to reading.

routing.rulesComment: Rules marked exact are exact commands and always apply; the others only decide when the router has no embedding model (with one, the examples below decide).

routing.argumentChecksComment: A tool argument checked by meaning before the tool runs: closer to invalid than valid examples (by margin) -> message is said instead.

tools.name: get_calories_today
tools.description: Read the user's calorie tracker: today's total and entries.

tools.name: log_food
tools.description: Log something the user says they ate or drank ('I ate', 'I had', 'log', 'add'). Give the food name and quantity; the app knows the calories of common foods. Set calories only if the user said a number.

food.description: Food or drink in the user's own Portuguese words, singular, e.g. ovo, banana, fatia de pizza, lata de refrigerante. Use 'calories' if the user only said a number.

calories.description: Total calories, only if the user said the number

tools.name: delete_food
tools.description: Delete a food or drink from today's list ('remove the kiwi', 'delete the coke', 'I didn't eat the banana').

food.description: The food to delete in the user's own words, e.g. kiwi, or 'last' for the last one

tools.name: remove_calories
tools.description: Subtract a number of calories from today's total ('remove 100 calories'). To remove a food, use delete_food.

tools.name: set_calories_today
tools.description: Replace today's total with an exact number, e.g. 'set it to 1500', 'reset to zero', 'today I ate 1200 in total'.

tools.name: undo_last_change
tools.description: Undo the last change to the calorie tracker ('undo', 'that was wrong', 'cancel that').

tools.name: correct_entry
tools.description: Fix a food already logged today: its amount ('I said one egg, not two') or the food itself ('it was a banana, not an apple').

food.description: The logged food to fix, in the user's words, e.g. ovo or maçã

new_food.description: The right food, only if the food itself was wrong, in the user's words, e.g. banana

matching.lastEntry: ^\s*(it|that|this|(the )?(last|latest|previous)( one| thing| item| entry| food)?)\s*$|\b(last|latest|previous) (one|thing|item|entry|food)\b|\b(remove|delete|erase) (it|that|this)\b|^\s*(?:isso|isto|(?:o |a )?(?:ultim|últim)[oa](?: coisa| item| registro| comida)?)\s*$|\b(?:remov(?:a|e)|apag(?:a|ue)|tir(?:a|e)) (?:isso|isto)\b
matching.correctionCuesComment: In a correction, the food (and count) right after one of these words is the logged one to fix ('a tea, not a coffee', 'one egg, not two'); another food named is the new one. The user's words win over the model's arguments.
matching.modifierCutsComment: A food's main part ends before these words ('coffee with milk' -> coffee); the known food must be the last word(s) of that part ('strawberry yogurt' -> yogurt, never strawberries). No known food there: it is looked up online, not guessed.
matching.routingMaskComment: With the embedding model, every known food name becomes this word in the routing examples and in the user's words, so the router decides by what the user wants, not by which food was named ('I did not say yogurt' is a complaint, not a log).

fallbackArguments.comment: When the model doesn't call log_food after a retry, the food (and count) come from the user's words: these patterns are removed (after the grams), then a leading count is read
